title: Plain milk for sour milk or buttermilk that baking soda depends on

evidence.basis: Knowledge packet 2026-10-13 item E3, PROPOSED (not approved). Research plain_milk_for_buttermilk_with_soda (SOURCE_SUPPORTED): King Arthur SRC-CM-26#f (don't use plain milk with soda), SRC-CM-26#e (soda-leavened cake darker and denser with plain milk), SRC-CM-26#d (plain-milk pancakes rose less); SRC-CM-35#a, SRC-CM-15#f (soda needs acid). Scope: baking soda in the recipe (applicability). Known conflict kept: King Arthur says a small amount (1/4 cup in a chocolate cake) can probably be swapped; no source gives a threshold.

text: Plain milk can't stand in for it as it is: the baking soda works by reacting with its acid, and without that it rises less and comes out darker and denser. Milk soured with lemon juice does the job.
scopeNote: About plain milk for all of it where the recipe's baking soda relies on its acid. King Arthur notes a small amount can probably be swapped, but no source gives a limit.
answer: on its own can't give the baking soda its acid
